items.title: 68145_Jimmie Rowles oral history interview
items.q: And they were my best friends! I liked them better than I liked anybody in the whole school.

ctx.x: Then I met this Indian, Blackfoot Indian out at Gonzaga University when I was studying pre-law. He was a musician, a real one. He was a genius. He came from a reservation, and nobody knows where he learned everything. But he played tenor saxophone, and he wrote arrangements without scores, and he had perfect pitch. He didn't a piano, it didn't mean anything to him. It was there in his head. And he heard me playing; I was trying to play like Freddie Kreitzer with Lombardo. I was in the gymnasium one day, playing.…

He'd come over there on a scholarship. They had brought about six Indians over there -- some Sioux, Blackfoot, Nez Perce(?)... And they were my best friends! I liked them better than I liked anybody in the whole school.

And I remember Tony Canadeo(?) was there when I was there. Years and years later, I was in Los Angeles, and I was playing with my trio, and the team that he was playing was... What was it? The one that won for so many years. Canadeo and the big-time coach that was such a wheel... Bart Starr...you know who I'm talking about. Detroit? No, it
